subject: Renewal: Dedicated capacity + autoscale policy adjustments

From: Sophia Chen <sophia@pacificai.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal conversation + capacity ask

Hi Logan,

Our contract with Redwood is up for renewal in August. We've seen steady growth on our real-time inference workload and want to discuss increasing our Dedicated pool alongside a few autoscale policy changes so we can avoid throttling during spikes.

High-level ask: add +16 A100-equivalent GPUs reserved for peak traffic, keep a warm pool to shave cold-starts (want <20s scale-up lag), and a contractual throughput floor of 3500 tokens/sec for our busiest model.

Can you share what a revised term would look like and whether we can lock those autoscale parameters into the renewal? Attachment: current utilization and projections (see throughput_calc.xlsx).

Thanks,
Sophia Chen
CTO, Pacific AI
ops@pacificai.com

- Reserved capacity: adding 16 A100-equivalent GPUs is doable; we'll profile the models to confirm equivalence and pricing.

Logging an initial technical readout — I'll run a short validation against Pacific's sample traces today. Early thoughts:

- The "+16 A100-eq" ask maps to either 4x p4d or 8x A10g-style nodes depending on batching. Need to confirm model size and max sequence length.
- Warm pool sizing: a warm pool of 3 replicas should reduce median cold-start to <12s and 95th percentile to ~25s in our env; warm pool uses reserved capacity, so it factors into committed GPU counts.
- Autoscale min/max: propose min_replicas=4, max_replicas=40 initially; we can tune after two weeks of telemetry.
- Scale-up policy: recommend proactive pre-warm when queue exceeds X tokens/sec for >30s and reactive scale with transient buffer to avoid oscillation (scale cooldown 60s).

I'll distill the validation and recommend a final config in the working session. If Pacific wants the throughput guarantee baked into the SOW, we should include an agreed measurement window and credits scheme.

Cheers,
Karthik Iyer
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Logan / team — thanks for the quick replies. A few clarifications from our side after reviewing the draft:

- Model footprint: two production models (gpt-like decoder ~10B params, and a smaller 3B reranker). Median seq len ~512, bursts up to 2048.
- Preferred reserved uplift: +16 A100-eq as you called out, but we want at least 6 GPUs dedicated to the warm pool (to support multiple hot models). If warm pool counts against reserved commit that's fine — we expect that in heavy hours the warm pool will reduce expensive scale operations.
- Autoscale policy: we want min_replicas set to 6 (to preserve steady-state latency), max_replicas to 64 for peak days, and an explicit max_scale_up_rate of +8 replicas per minute to avoid noisy neighbor issues.

Also: Pacific is willing to accept a 95% throughput SLA (measured on 1-hour windows) at 3500 tokens/sec in exchange for a 12‑month committed term at the revised pricing. If missed, a credit of 10% of the monthly committed fee per missed window.

Let's discuss tomorrow at 10am PT.

—Sophia
CTO, Pacific AI
